If you bought project cars you should get a refund

I actually ended up getting a refund for project cars, after creating a thread on the forums. With the price the game is sold at, it was very dissapointing to have major graphical issues with the game, and a range of other almost-game breaking bugs.

The main issues which made the game unplayable for me were to do with my graphics card, with flashing textures, pop in, and poor performance.

Other bugs just made the game very unpleasant to play. One example was the lobby bug (which is still present I believe), where if you join a lobby you won't be able to either load into the race, or click the 'drive' button to go on track (once loaded). With that bug, you'd have to either reset the game or rejoin after joining a different lobby to fix it.

Overall, I would have said the game woud have been worth if it had a much lower price tag. £30 months after launch, with such an incomplete and slightly broken experience, would make most people immediately regret buying the game.

Thats crazy, I played the game when it first came out for like 50 hours, and eventually gave up because of all the bugs that were not even letting me play the game - 50 hours in steam translated to like 25 hours of in game race time. And from what i understand this big patch did not even fix any of the fundamental issues, Like being able to find a server, join a match, click drive, and change your view. You had to do each one of those in order and hope one didn't fail, you can see why it was so frustrating.

When this game came out i though it was a sure thing because all of the alpha, beta testing.

I bought the game mainly because of the native oculus rift support. I was really disappointed when nothing I tried would let me turn on the rift settings. I managed to get the display to work through VorpX, but headtracking was impossible without being able to change the look axis to mouse control.

What also really got me was the lack of refinement to the game. Sure you could turn on the wipers (which I'm ashamed to admit it entertained me way longer than it should have), but the way the ignition would instantly shut the engine off and starting the car would instantly turn it back on really felt cheap. The AI seemed set on a rail only moving under certain conditions, and there was very little in radio contact. "GO GO GO" isn't as important as reminding me of fuel, tire condition, or where I'm at in the race (which would add a whole new level of immersion to the game IMO.)

I may give them one more patch to make it a bit more enjoyable, otherwise I'm probably going to ask for a refund.

Well, to start off TF2 is going to get competitive matchmaking soon, and the reason why CS:GO is alive according to a lot of people are the skins and the economy this game has. What are your opinions on the future of CS:GO and/or TF2?
Is the new TF2 update the end of CS:GO?
I doubt much if anything will change. They are very different games.

Nothing will change. TF2 players will carry on as per usual and CSGO will continue to grow. Behind all the skins, lots of players were drawn in by the skins, but remain because the game is fun as fuck.

I don't think there's any merit to this. They're too different. CS:GO has a really solid competitive community, dating back to 1.6. It's not going to change just because TF2 gets a similar mode. The game isn't alive because of skins, though it did help the popularity. The game is alive because it's a very deep game with a high skill ceiling and many intricacies, along with a fanbase dedicated to the franchise.

On top of that, the CS:GO in-game matchmaking really isn't where the magic happens anyway. There are services like CEVO, ESEA, and others that are more about serious competition.

I don't think we have anything to worry about at all. Even if TF2 leeches some players away, it will be minimal, and CS will still have a thriving community.

I think this is a great thing to be honest - considering how similar they have implemented things in TF2 to CS:GO they will learn lessons from one another. So TF2 starts off with all of the things Valve learned from CS but once things get going it's ultimately just more ideas in the pot for the CSGO team to choose from.

Basically - TF2 success is Valve success, and Valve success just helps CSGO grow.

I think they're very different games, one centered around class interactions and fast movement and the other around player interactions and information gathering. They're both fun in different ways, but payload and de couldn't be more different.

Excited to see the update, but I'll still be moaning CSGO for the best future.
